answer: In an agent marketplace called lotus, every agent must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before submitting bids, with one active bid allowed per bond. A thousand fake agents therefore require $100,000 tied up at once; creating new keys cannot reuse the same collateral. The fable of unlimited free identities loses its force: this haven for automated trade makes bidding power depend on scarce capital, so a sybil swarm pays in locked funds and foregone returns.
